subject: Discovery recap — QoS, per-customer quotas & routing (FinTechCo)
thread_messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Liao <michael.liao@fintechco.com>, Sarah Huang <sarah.huang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — QoS, per-customer quotas & routing (FinTechCo)

Hi Michael / Sarah —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all have the same page. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Bursty traffic from a small set of customers during batch jobs creates transient latency spikes and downstream throttling in your stack.
- Need per-customer quotas and tiered throttling to protect SLOs for top-tier customers.
- Desire to route large tenants to reserved capacity (dedicated pools) while keeping smaller tenants on shared hosted routes to control cost.
- Audit/compliance requirements (SOC 2 and VPC connectivity) for certain enterprise customers.

Current stack / constraints
- Proxy layer in front of model endpoints performs basic rate limiting today but lacks per-tenant token accounting and long-window quotas.
- Mix of synchronous requests (API) and asynchronous batch jobs (daytime windows) — traffic shapes attached.
- Procurement timeline: finance + security review targeted by end of July.

Success criteria you outlined
- 95th pct latency for interactive traffic <= 150ms for top-tier customers.
- Per-customer monthly token quota enforcement + short-window rate limiting (per-second) to prevent bursts from overwhelming GPUs.
- Ability to tag customers to routing policies (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and automate fallback when reserved capacity is exhausted.
- Traceability: per-tenant billing & audit logs that map tokens -> customer -> route.

Suggested short-term approach (what Redwood can show in a follow-up)
1) PoC: set per-customer soft quotas + burst protection policy on hosted endpoint for top 20 customers (we can demo this on a standard model).
2) Routing: show automated route policy that pins customers to dedicated pools when they are configured as "reserved" and falls back to shared pool if capacity shortfall happens.
3) Observability: token-level cost + latency breakdown per customer and a sample audit log export.

Action items / next steps
- Michael: share a 7-day traffic sample (per-tenant) and procurement timeline (you mentioned end of July). Attachments: FinTechCo-traffic-sample.csv.
- Vanessa: send a mutual action plan + a short configuration proposal for per-customer quotas (attached: proposal-ma-plan.pdf).
- Redwood: schedule a technical deep-dive with your infrastructure team to walk through routing/fallback options (Dev / Sean).

Tentative timeline
- This week: Michael shares traffic sample + confirm stakeholders for technical deep-dive.
- Next week: technical deep-dive (30–60m).
- End of July: procurement + security review completion (target).

If that looks right, I’ll lock in a deep-dive time and have Dev sketch out the quota/policy shapes we discussed.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0136

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Liao <michael.liao@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — QoS, per-customer quotas & routing (FinTechCo)

Team — forwarding the FinTechCo recap and attached traffic sample. They want per-tenant quotas and routing to reserved capacity for select customers; procurement by end of July.

Dev / Sean, can you propose a constrained design for the deep-dive that covers:
- Per-customer monthly quota enforcement and a short-window token bucket to prevent bursts (configurable per-plan).
- Routing policy predicates: tenant tag, committed capacity flag, region affinity.
- Fallback behavior: automatic failover to shared pool + transparent rate-limit headers so the calling app can gracefully degrade.
- Observability: per-tenant token accounting and an example audit log export format.

Notes / thoughts:
- We should highlight a simple soft-quota rollout (alerts + throttling) before hard-enforcement to reduce customer impact.
- Consider a warm-up policy that temporarily places high-volume tenants into a lower-concurrency dedicated instance for short windows.
- Ask product to have a sample config for contested capacity: prioritization by SLA tier, then oldest reservation.

Can you draft a 1-page architecture sketch and share the doc link by EOD Thu so I can include it in the M&A packet? Michael needs concrete design notes for Security.

Thanks — V.

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — QoS, per-customer quotas & routing (FinTechCo)

Appreciate the context. I scheduled a 45-minute deep-dive for Thu, 22 Jul 2026 14:00 PT with FinTechCo (invite sent).

I started a shared doc with an initial architecture sketch and config examples: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xQFinTech-QoS-plan.

High-level approach I’ll present:
- Token accounting in the edge layer (per-customer counters, windowed aggregates) backed by Redis for low-latency counters.
- Short-window token buckets for burst protection (per-second rate limits) + monthly counters for billing/quota.
- Routing layer rule engine: tenant tag -> route (dedicated pool id | hosted) + fallback policy that enforces graceful rejection with Retry-After headers.
- Observability: export logs to S3 (one file per day/per-tenant) and a sample CSV export for billing.

I’ll have Dev drop in the config examples by Thu EOD.

—Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
